name: Autosomal Recessive Congenital Myasthenic Syndrome Due to Defective Synaptic Vesicles Exocytosis
aliases: AR CMS with Synaptic Vesicle Exocytosis Defect
Congenital Myasthenic Syndrome Type Synaptic Vesicle Defect

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Congenital Myasthenic Syndromes

criteria.description: Presence of fatigable muscle weakness with onset in infancy or early childhood
Electromyography showing decremental response on repetitive nerve stimulation
Identification of biallelic pathogenic variants in genes affecting synaptic vesicle exocytosis (e.g., SYT2, SNAP25)
Improvement of symptoms with acetylcholinesterase inhibitors or 3,4-diaminopyridine
Muscle biopsy showing normal morphology or mild nonspecific changes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical presentation plus electrophysiological evidence and confirmation by genetic testing
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic confirmation is essential due to phenotypic overlap with other neuromuscular disorders.

searchTerms: muscle weakness that worsens with use

pathognomonic.symptomName: Impaired neuromuscular transmission evidenced by decremental EMG response
searchTerms: muscle weakness from nerve signal problems

common.symptomName: Bulbar muscle weakness causing dysarthria and dysphagia
searchTerms: weak throat muscles causing speech and swallowing issues
bulbar weakness with dysarthria and dysphagia
difficulty speaking and swallowing from muscle weakness

common.symptomName: Respiratory muscle weakness leading to episodic respiratory insufficiency
searchTerms: weak breathing muscles causing breathing problems
episodes of respiratory failure from muscle weakness
respiratory insufficiency due to weak muscles

common.notes: Helps differentiate from other neuromuscular disorders

searchTerms: slight loss of muscle bulk in arms or legs
mild autonomic symptoms like dry mouth

rare.symptomName: Severe respiratory failure requiring mechanical ventilation

imaging: Muscle MRI may show mild fatty infiltration in chronic cases
Chest imaging to assess respiratory complications
genetic: Biallelic pathogenic variants in genes involved in synaptic vesicle exocytosis such as SYT2, SNAP25, or related genes
other: Electrophysiological studies showing decremental response on repetitive nerve stimulation
Normal muscle biopsy or mild nonspecific changes

distinguishingFeatures: Different genetic mutations affecting postsynaptic or basal lamina proteins
Progressive muscle atrophy without neuromuscular junction transmission defect
Genetic testing for SMN1 gene deletion

redFlags: Severe bulbar weakness causing aspiration risk
Lack of response to acetylcholinesterase inhibitors
